sentences.text: Meterchen is a newly described genus and species that is currently regarded as a valid taxon.
The genus name alludes to the Mother Goose nursery rhyme about a goose rising from the mud.
Only a single species, Meterchen luti, is known from the record.
The taxon was formally described by Alan J. D. Tennyson and colleagues.
Meterchen luti was named by Tennyson et al. in 2026.
The authors of the study include Tennyson, Steell, Lubbe, Adams, Greer, Brown, Wilson, Campbell, Dale, and Rawlence.
The description appeared in the journal Historical Biology.
Based on its morphology, Meterchen is interpreted as a probable goose, suggesting a herbivorous diet typical of waterfowl.
The type species of the genus is M. luti.
Meterchen lived during the Miocene epoch.
Its fossils come from the Bannockburn Formation, specifically the St Bathans deposits of New Zealand.
The specimens were recovered in New Zealand.
